slots.repairQuestion: If a behavior increases because it turns off an annoying alarm, is that reinforcement or punishment, and why?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says reinforcement because the behavior increases and the aversive stimulus is removed.

slots.repair: In this vocabulary, positive and negative refer to adding or removing a stimulus, not moral value or pleasantness.
slots.repairQuestion: What does positive mean in positive punishment?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says a stimulus is added, even if it is unpleasant.

slots.label: intention-over-effect
slots.description: A consequence is reinforcement if the teacher intended it as a reward, regardless of what happens to behavior.
slots.repair: Operant labels depend on the behavior's observed future change, not only the giver's intention.
slots.repairQuestion: If praise is intended as a reward but the behavior decreases, can we call it reinforcement based only on intention?
slots.repairCriteria: Repaired when the learner says classification depends on whether the behavior actually increases or decreases.

slots.text: Reinforcement and punishment are defined by behavioral effect: increase versus decrease. Positive and negative mean adding versus removing a stimulus. The common trap is treating negative reinforcement as punishment; it is reinforcement because it increases the behavior that removes or avoids an aversive condition.
